messages:
Noah Kim: hi all, first week here — got my env + tests passing. about to open my first PR. quick runbook: branch name, commit style, reviewer etiquette, and how we verify in staging?
Priya Rao: welcome Noah! :wave: Our branch pattern is `me/<initials>-<ticket>-<short>` for personal branches, e.g., `me/nk-4567-fix-typo`. For shared feature branches use `feat/<ticket>-<short>`.
Marco Silva: commit messages: we keep them simple but informative. Format we like: one-line header <=72 chars, blank line, short body. If it's a bugfix reference the issue: `Fixes: #NNN` if applicable. Example:
```
fix(storage): avoid double-free on cache close

Ensure cache.shutdown is idempotent to prevent crash on rapid restarts. Fixes: #4567
```
Noah Kim: thanks — do we squash on merge?
Priya Rao: generally squash for feature/fix PRs. For release branches we preserve merge commits. Also add a changelog line if the change affects user-facing behaviour (in the PR description under "Changelog").
Noah Kim: who should I request for reviews as a newcomer?
Marco Silva: request the path owner + a buddy. If you're unsure, ping `@eng` or `@devex` and ask for a first-timer pair review. For infra changes request `@eng-infra`. We try to get at least 2 reviewers for anything touching core libs.
Repo Bot: [automated] tip: use the PR template. Include the short motivation, testing steps, and the `staging-preview` link if the deploy runs.
Noah Kim: how do I run the staging preview locally?
Priya Rao: we have a lightweight staging preview for web changes — put `preview: true` in the PR body and CI will create a deploy. For backend changes run the smoke harness: `./dev/run-smoke --mini` then `make test-integration`.
Noah Kim: commands I ran: `make setup && pre-commit run --all-files && pytest -q` — is that sufficient?
Marco Silva: yep. Also run the e2e subset for any API changes: `./scripts/e2e --tag quick`. If CI flakes, include the CI output in the PR and mark with `ci:flaky` label.
Build Bot: [automated] CI passed: unit (✓), lint (✓), typecheck (✓), integration (skipped). See https://ci.example.com/1972345678
Noah Kim: any labels I should attach before requesting review?
Priya Rao: add one of: `type/bug`, `type/feat`, or `type/chore`, plus `release/next` if it should be included in the upcoming release. For backports add `backport-request`. If you want a quick turnaround add `review/fast`.
Noah Kim: how strict are we on changing formatting or imports?
Marco Silva: prefer tiny PRs. If it's only formatting run `pre-commit` and mark as `type/chore`. If you're touching behavior + formatting split into two PRs if possible.
Noah Kim: and rebasing / force-push etiquette?
Priya Rao: it's fine to rebase personal branches, but if others are reviewing don't force-push without warning. If you rebase, add a short note in the PR timeline.
Noah Kim: last one: is there a checklist I should paste into the PR body?
Marco Silva: yup, use this minimal checklist in PR description:
- Motivation and summary
- Testing steps and local commands
- CI status (link)
- Reviewers requested
- Changelog entry if needed
- `preview: true` if you want the staging preview

Noah Kim: perfect, thanks — I'll open a draft PR and ping @Priya and @Marco for an initial pass.
Priya Rao: happy to pair-review your first PR. Ping me when it's ready.
Build Bot: [automated] reminder: run `pre-commit` hooks locally to avoid iteration cycle.
Noah Kim: thanks everyone — opening now :rocket:
